answer_text:
# 🏥 Medi-Cal: Overview & Key 2026 Changes

**Medi-Cal** is California's Medicaid program, providing **free or low-cost health coverage** to low-income individuals and families. Here is a comprehensive breakdown of what Medi-Cal is and the major changes happening in 2026 and beyond:

---

## 📋 What Is Medi-Cal?

Medi-Cal offers benefits like free or low-cost coverage for medical, dental, vision, prescription drugs, mental health, and more, including coverage for emergency services and hospitalization.

If your household income remains within Medi-Cal's income threshold (currently about **$21,600 per year** for a single individual), your coverage will remain intact.

---

## 🔄 Major Medi-Cal Changes in 2026

### 1. 🛂 Immigration Status Restrictions (January 1, 2026)
Starting January 1, 2026, adults (ages 19 and older) who do not have satisfactory immigration status will **not be able to newly enroll** in full-scope Medi-Cal. If you already have Medi-Cal, you can keep it as long as you renew on time and use your benefits.

### 2. 💰 Asset Limit Returns (January 1, 2026)
Beginning January 1, 2026, California Medi-Cal will once again limit your countable assets to **$130,000 per person** and **$195,000 per couple**. From 2024 through 2025, Californians were able to qualify for Medi-Cal without worrying about how much they had saved — the removal of the asset test simplified the application process and reduced administrative burdens.

In 2026, Medi-Cal will conduct **redeterminations**, where many individuals will suddenly exceed the asset limit and receive a "Notice of Action" ending their Medi-Cal benefits.

### 3. 🦷 Dental Coverage Changes (July 1, 2026)
Starting July 1, 2026, some Medi-Cal members will **stop getting full-scope dental services** as part of their Medi-Cal coverage. This primarily affects undocumented adults ages 19 and older.

### 4. 📋 Income Verification (2026)
Beginning in 2026, the state will require **twice-yearly income verification** to confirm eligibility. Those who qualify will continue receiving free or low-cost health coverage.

---

## 📅 Coming Changes in 2027 & Beyond

### Work Requirements (January 1, 2027)
Starting January 1, 2027, some adults will need to **work, volunteer, or go to school** to keep Medi-Cal. Exemptions include:
Children (0–18), older adults (65+), pregnant people (including one year postpartum), parents with children ages 0–13, people with disabilities, and people with serious health or mental health conditions.

### Semi-Annual Renewals (January 1, 2027)
Starting January 1, 2027, some Medi-Cal members will have their eligibility checked **twice a year** instead of once. You may need to renew your Medi-Cal every six months — missing deadlines could cause loss of coverage.

### Copayments (October 1, 2028)
Starting October 1, 2028, some adults on Medi-Cal may have to pay a **small fee (copayment)** for certain services.

---

## ✅ What You Should Do Now

- **Renew on time** — always read and respond to mail from Medi-Cal or your county.
- If you forget to renew your Medi-Cal or missed your date, you have a **90-day Grace Period** from the last date of eligibility to renew and keep your current benefits.
- If your income rises above Medi-Cal's threshold, you won't lose access to health insurance — you'll simply transition into a private plan through **Covered California**, where federal and state subsidies keep plans highly affordable, often at $0 monthly premiums.
- You can apply or manage your Medi-Cal at **BenefitsCal.com** or by contacting your local county Medi-Cal office.

---
